````markdown
**Never take this path on a host that has ever run with `BILLING_STAGE_CLOCK_OFFSET_DAYS`** (the sandbox run of §14.9
sets it, which is why that run has a server of its own). Such a host holds billing rows and queued jobs dated up to a
month ahead, and once it pointed at live those jobs would wait and then run against the live services. Destroy that
server instead (§14.9, step 8), and go live on a host whose billing clock never moved. The API refuses to start
pointed at live while any billing row or open billing job is dated more than one day ahead, and prints
`BILLING_RECORDS_DATED_AHEAD` with two counts (`rows=` and `jobs=`). That is only a safety net: a month after such a
run nothing is ahead any more, so the check cannot replace this rule.

The path is for a host that used NETOPIA's sandbox on the real clock only, for example a quick look at the checkout
before go-live. The sandbox and live are two separate NETOPIA systems, and the live site never renews a sandbox plan,
so a sandbox plan left open would stay active for ever. So, while the host still points at the sandbox:

1. Sign in as each sandbox test account and cancel its plan in Settings (or withdraw it, within 14 days). A cancelled
   plan whose month has not ended yet is fine: it is never renewed.
   If a sandbox withdrawal was handed to you (the quarterly summary lists it as `WITHDRAWAL_BY_OWNER`), settle it now,
   while the host still points at the sandbox, with `pnpm billing:withdraw --owner ... --refund ... --dashboard ...`
   (see "A withdrawal sent by email or on the model form" below).

2. Wait until every sandbox charge has an outcome, and every refund, invoice and credit note a sandbox charge queued
   has run. The payment checks run every few minutes, and the status reads of §14.8's journal table find a charge
   whose message never came.
   An invoice or credit note that keeps failing is tried again after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 12 hours, and then given up.
   A payment check is given up after at most about 31 hours.
   A refund handed to you in the sandbox (O2_REFUND_DUE) stays open until you record it: refund it in the sandbox admin and record it, as **A refund handed to you** below says, before the switch.

```sh
sudo -u postgres psql -d debateai -c "SELECT count(*) AS open_sandbox_subscriptions FROM billing.subscription_latest_v s JOIN billing.subscription_event c ON c.subscription_id = s.subscription_id AND c.kind = 'CREATED' WHERE jsonb_extract_path_text(c.data, 'payment_environment') = 'sandbox' AND s.kind NOT IN ('ENDED', 'WITHDRAWN', 'ERASURE_STOPPED', 'CANCEL_REQUESTED')"
```

```sh
sudo -u postgres psql -d debateai -c "SELECT count(*) AS open_sandbox_charges FROM billing.charge c WHERE c.payment_environment = 'sandbox' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM billing.charge_event f WHERE f.charge_id = c.charge_id AND f.kind IN ('SUCCEEDED', 'FAILED')) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM billing.subscription_latest_v s WHERE s.subscription_id = c.subscription_id AND s.kind IN ('ENDED', 'WITHDRAWN'))"
```

```sh
sudo -u postgres psql -d debateai -c "SELECT count(*) AS open_sandbox_jobs FROM billing.outbox j WHERE j.done_at IS NULL AND j.dead_at IS NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM billing.charge c WHERE c.payment_environment = 'sandbox' AND (c.charge_id = jsonb_extract_path_text(j.payload, 'charge_id') OR c.charge_id = j.ref))"
```

The third counts the sandbox jobs still queued: the refunds, invoices and credit notes of sandbox charges, and the
payment checks that name a sandbox charge. Once the host points at live, the live site would take such a job. It
would end it without calling any service
(the site refuses a refund, invoice, credit note or payment check of another payment system),
but the start-up check below still refuses to start while any is left, so the switch is never made with sandbox work

```

```sh

```

```sh
systemctl restart debateai-api
```

The API checks this itself at start-up: pointed at live while a sandbox plan, charge or queued job is still open, it
refuses to start and prints `BILLING_OTHER_SYSTEM_RECORDS_OPEN` with the three counts. The first query can count a

The sandbox plans and charges stay in the database, but they never count as sales:
the quarterly tax summary and its email read only live charges.
````

(g) `**A refund that could not be completed.**` (the whole paragraph to the line before `**When xMoney or the tax
service is down at a renewal.**`) is replaced by:

````markdown
**A refund handed to you.** NETOPIA has not yet confirmed its refund call for our account, so every refund the site
owes (a withdrawal, a card from a blocked country, a second payment, an upgrade that can no longer be given) is made by
you in NETOPIA's admin. The site emails you at once (O2_REFUND_DUE, "A refund is due: make it in NETOPIA's admin") with
the reason, our charge reference, NETOPIA's payment number, the exact amount and currency, whether it is the whole
payment, for a withdrawal the date the law requires it by (14 days after the person withdrew), and, for a part of a
payment, the one command to run once it is done. Look at that payment in NETOPIA's admin first. If it already shows a
refund of that amount, an earlier refund went through: never refund it again. If not, refund exactly the amount the
email names, on that payment, in one refund. A whole refund is recorded by the site itself as soon as NETOPIA reports
it: the person's email (M8 or M11) and the credit note follow by themselves. A part of a payment is recorded only when
you run the command from the email, because NETOPIA has not said whether it reports the amount of a partial refund.
The command shows first what it will record and what the person will read, and records nothing:

```sh
# Paste the charge reference from the email and press Enter; then the amount you refunded, exactly as the email names it (for example 12.10), and press Enter.
read -r CHARGE_REF && read -r AMOUNT && systemd-run --pipe --wait --collect --uid=debateai-api --gid=debateai-api --property=EnvironmentFile=/etc/debateai/api.env --working-directory=/opt/debateai/dialectical-engine /usr/bin/pnpm billing:refund-done --charge "$CHARGE_REF" --amount "$AMOUNT"
```

Then run it again with `--confirm` to record it:

```sh
# Paste the charge reference from the email and press Enter; then the amount you refunded, exactly as the email names it (for example 12.10), and press Enter.
read -r CHARGE_REF && read -r AMOUNT && systemd-run --pipe --wait --collect --uid=debateai-api --gid=debateai-api --property=EnvironmentFile=/etc/debateai/api.env --working-directory=/opt/debateai/dialectical-engine /usr/bin/pnpm billing:refund-done --charge "$CHARGE_REF" --amount "$AMOUNT" --confirm
```

It prints one line saying what it recorded. A refusal is one code and nothing is written: `BILLING_REFUND_DONE_USAGE`
(run it again as shown), `BILLING_REFUND_DONE_CHARGE_NOT_FOUND` (paste the reference again exactly as the email names
it), `BILLING_REFUND_DONE_OTHER_PAYMENT_SYSTEM` (the charge was paid in another payment system than this host's:
nothing to record here), `BILLING_REFUND_DONE_NO_OPEN_REQUEST` (no refund is open on that charge: it is already
recorded), `BILLING_REFUND_DONE_EXCEEDS_REQUEST` (the amount is more than the refund still open: check the email and
the admin), `BILLING_REFUND_DONE_FAILED` (the command could not finish; run it again later, and if it repeats tell
whoever runs the server). Until a refund is recorded, the daily summary reminds you of it (O2_REFUND_REMINDER) on the
day it becomes due, then every third day, and every day from three days before a withdrawal's deadline.

A refund for another reason code needs no refund on this host. `REFUND_NOT_REQUESTED`: that refund job matches no
refund request our records hold for the payment. `REFUND_CHARGE_MISSING`: the job names a charge we do not have. For
either, do not refund it, and do not treat its amount as owed. Something able to write to the billing database queued
it, so tell whoever runs the server; they check that charge's own refund requests (a request that was never refunded
is still owed). The email says the same for both, and the owner summary lists both as `REFUND_NOT_REQUESTED`.
The reason code `OTHER_PAYMENT_SYSTEM` means the payment was taken in another payment system than the one this host
uses (NETOPIA's other environment, or the previous card processor): nothing was sent and nothing is owed on this host.
Its email has no refund reason and no deadline paragraph, and the owner summary lists it as `REFUND_OTHER_SYSTEM`. If
it was a real customer's payment in the other system, refund it in that system's admin; a sandbox test payment needs
nothing.
````

## Part C — Prices in RON, EUR and USD, by region

Part C was revised on 10 October 2026; its task texts are the SDD briefs C0–C4; spec §2.16 is the design.

The owner's choice of 9–10 October 2026 (ruling PR-60) sells all three currencies at once, by the buyer's tax country
(RON for Romania; EUR for the other 26 EU countries and NO, IS, LI, CH and GB; USD elsewhere), and NETOPIA's answers of
9 October (ruling PR-61) are in spec §2.24. The drafted tasks C1–C4 that stood here (one currency published at a time,
and a refused plan change across currencies) are superseded and removed from this plan; they remain in its history.
The briefs are `task-C0-brief.md` … `task-C4-brief.md` in the SDD folder (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-05-netopia-switch/`),
each complete on its own beside `global-constraints.md` and `binding-rulings.md`; `task-C5-brief.md` is the
controller's final review, records and pull request. Spec §2.16.9 lists what each task does, and §2.25 is the decision
log.

Build order: **C0 → C1 → C2 → C3 → C4 → C5** (controller).

## Appendix A — Controller rulings (binding)

Binding for every implementer, reviewer and judge of this program, beside the spec
(`dialectical-engine/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-netopia-payments-design.md`), the plan's header and the interface
contract (`plan-facts/PLAN-SKELETON.md`). Later sections win over earlier ones; this file wins over a task text where they
differ. Each ruling: what — why — cost if wrong.

## Rulings on the drafted task texts (6–7 October 2026)

- **PR-1 (build order).** N24 (the cross-flow harnesses on NETOPIA) runs **before** N23 (removing xMoney): tests are
  typechecked, and `tests/support/billingStack.ts`, `billingHarness.ts` and `apps/runner/src/dev-billing-fakes.ts` import
  the xMoney fake and package until N24 rewrites them. Build order: … N21 → N22 → **N24 → N23** → N25. — Why: N23 cannot keep
  `pnpm run typecheck` green otherwise (N23's own note). — Cost if wrong: one reordering.
- **PR-2 (the xMoney members of the connectors, N8).** Until N23, with billing on and no `XMONEY_*` settings, the xMoney
  members of `BillingConnectors` are an inert stand-in (a random held key, a client whose `fetch` answers 429 so every call
  is `XMONEY_UNAVAILABLE`, `xmoneyEnvironment: "stage"`), so the not-yet-switched files keep their types. N23 removes them.
  — Why: the skeleton's "billing-on no longer requires the xMoney group" without a type churn in 14 files. — Cost if wrong:
  none in production (billing stays off).
- **PR-3 (detail suffixes, N8).** `BILLING_IPN_KEYS_FILE_UNSAFE` carries a detail (`:ABSENT`, `:NOT_A_FILE`, `:TOO_LARGE`,
  `:WRITABLE_BY_API_USER`, `:NOT_ROOT_OWNED`, `:GROUP_OR_OTHER_WRITABLE`), like `NETOPIA_IPN_KEYS_INVALID:<why>`. — Why:
  the owner sees what to fix. — Cost if wrong: none.
- **PR-4 (the example environment, N8).** `deploy/vps/env/api.env.example` ships NETOPIA's four lines commented out, with
  the guided setup as the way to fill them. — Why: four set lines with billing off would switch the provider-only mode on
  for any fresh hosted install. — Cost if wrong: none.
- **PR-5 (the owner commands' environment).** `parseBillingWithdrawEnvironment` and `parseBillingInvoiceEnvironment`
  switch from `XMONEY_API_BASE_URL` to `NETOPIA_API_BASE_URL` in **N23** (Step 9 (d)); N14 does not touch them. Until N23
  those two commands refuse to start on an `api.env` without the xMoney line, which affects no running server (billing is
  off everywhere). — Why: one owner for the change. — Cost if wrong: none.
- **PR-6 (O3 generalised once, by its first raiser).** O3's subject and intro become provider-neutral ("Billing needs your
  attention ({reasonCode})"), with the `paymentAlert` flag N11's text defines, in the **first** task in build order that
  raises a payment alert (N9: `NOTICE_PARSE_FAILED`). Later tasks (N10, N11, …) reuse it; a later task's own O3 template
  edit becomes a check that the generalised O3 is in place. — Why: one template version; N9 and N10 run before N11. — Cost
  if wrong: a template conflict at merge time.
- **PR-7 (the payer helpers).** `apps/api/src/billing/netopia-payer.ts` (`payerFromProfile`, `clientIdOf`,
  `netopiaNotifyUrl`, `paymentReturnUrl`) is created by the first task that needs it in build order and reused by every later
  one (N11, N12, N13, N18). If an earlier task (N9, N10) already created the same helper under another name, the earlier
  name wins and N11's text adapts. — Why: one source for the notify and return addresses. — Cost if wrong: duplication.
- **PR-8 (one "this payment system" predicate, revised after the drafts).** Until N23 the predicate is N11's
  `servedHere(row, systems)` with `PaymentSystems` (`apps/api/src/billing/renewal-rules.ts`), serving both systems;
  wrappers such as N12's `servedByNetopia` call it. If a task before N11 in build order needs the predicate, it creates
  `servedHere`/`PaymentSystems` there with N11's exact text, and N11's step becomes a check. N23 replaces every
  `servedHere(row, systems)` call with N23's `isThisPaymentSystem(row, environment)` (NETOPIA only) and deletes
  `servedHere` and `PaymentSystems`. The job-level DEAD helper is `otherPaymentSystem(audit, kind)` (N10 creates it in
  `outbox.ts`; N23 keeps that one copy). — Why: one rule per era, no duplicates after N23. — Cost if wrong: duplication.
- **PR-9 (credentials refusals alert the owner).** A renewal's `CHARGE_CREDENTIALS_REFUSED` raises O3 too (spec §2.9.2),
  beside `CHARGE_CONFIGURATION_REFUSED`. — Why: the spec says so; the skeleton's list was short. — Cost if wrong: one extra
  owner email per code and hour.
- **PR-10 (unknown outcomes, N11).** A status read that fails during §2.9.3 is resent after 30 quiet minutes, as a
  `NO_SUCH_ORDER` is; at the window's end only a fresh `NO_SUCH_ORDER` or a final unpaid state closes the attempt; a
  SUBMITTED renewal whose deadline read answers `NO_SUCH_ORDER` closes `FAILED(NO_TRANSACTION)` with the audit code
  `PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND`. — Why: spec §2.9.3 step 2 and the safe side at step 4. — Cost if wrong: a later close.
- **PR-11 (a 56 answer, revised after the drafts).** N3's `answeredOrderReused(report)` (a module-level WeakSet in the
  NETOPIA package) is the flag; there is no `onOrderReused` hook. (a) **N11** writes the content-free audit line
  `billing.payment.order_reused {orderId}` and raises O3 `ORDER_REUSED` when the answer to a renewal's **first** send is
  flagged (spec §2.4.3's anomaly); the answer to a resend (§2.9.3 step 2) is expected to be flagged and writes nothing.
  (b) A `56` on `startHostedPayment` is `PAYMENT_CONFIGURATION_REFUSED:56` (N2/N3), which the checkout, the upgrade and the
  card change answer 503 and alert the owner (O3) for, like any configuration refusal. (c) Under the sandbox clock the
  flag is lost (`TimeShiftedCardPayments` copies the report): accepted, sandbox only. — Cost if wrong: one missed audit
  line in the sandbox.
- **PR-12 (N4's choices).** Accepted as written: the rejection-reason → SDK-code map (`NOTICE_HEADER_MISSING`,
  `NOTICE_ALG_REFUSED`, `NOTICE_ISSUER_INVALID` → 268435713); the key-list codes `NO_KEY`, `BLOCK_TYPE`,
  `BLOCK_UNTERMINATED`, `UNREADABLE`, `NOT_RSA`, `TOO_SHORT`; a key listed twice kept once; certificate dates not checked;
  the tolerant parse keeping any integer status 0–32,767; `message` kept only when 1–255 characters without control
  characters; `readable` false only for non-UTF-8 or non-object JSON. `NETOPIA_FACTS.tokenPaths` are dot paths from the
  body root (`"payment.binding.token"`, `"payment.instrument.token"`, `"payment.token"`); `netopiaCountryToIso2` accepts
  numeric text (`"642"`), numbers and alpha-2. — Cost if wrong: one constant.
- **PR-13 (the published key file).** The PEM in `deploy/vps/netopia/published-ipn-key.pem` is accepted because its SPKI
  SHA-256 matches `eeba3b06…78d7` (N4's test recomputes it from the file, so any altered byte fails the build). — Cost if
  wrong: none (the owner still confirms the key with NETOPIA, N-5).
- **PR-14 (N8's choices).** Accepted: base-URL and POS checks in `loadNetopiaConnectors` with payments-netopia's own
  functions (register does not depend on payments-netopia), still answering `BILLING_CONFIGURATION_INVALID:<KEY>`; the old
  stage-clock and invoicer-guard error codes and names kept (the runbook pins them; N25 may rename them with the runbook);
  N8 also touching `packages/db/src/billing.ts` (`openOtherSystemRecordCounts`), `tests/support/billingStack.ts`,
  `apps/runner/src/dev-billing-fakes.ts` and `tests/integration/dev-billing-fakes.test.ts`.
- **PR-15 (N23's choices).** Accepted: `SubscriptionState` loses `xmoneyOrderId`, `xmoneyCustomerId` and `cardRef` in N23
  (no reader is left; the columns stay); the "nothing named xMoney is left" guard pins each remaining mention with its
  reason (0087/0096 CHECK values, `RETIRED_OUTBOX_KINDS`, the old CREATED's `data.xmoney_environment`, the boot warning's
  key names, the migration suites' seeded old rows, the specs, this plan, `docs/missions/**`); stored `OTHER_XMONEY_SYSTEM`
  values are read through `otherSystemCode` (no migration); N23 rewrites O2's xMoney-dashboard sentences unless N14 already
  says "NETOPIA's admin".

## Rulings on the second drafting wave (7 October 2026)

- **PR-16 (O3, the payment alert, by build order).** N9 lands O3's generalised form (subject "Billing needs your attention
  ({reasonCode})", the `paymentAlert` flag, `SAMPLE.paymentAlert`, the subject pin and the "speaks of a payment" test, and

  (`queuePaymentAlert`) and SKIPS its own O3 template, `owner.json` and render-test edits (N9 made them). **N11** imports
  `queuePaymentAlert` from `./payment-alert.js` (it does not define one in `renewal.ts`), SKIPS its O3 template edits, and
  adds `confirmCard: "true"` to the render test's `SAMPLE`. — Why: one template version; build order N9 → N10 → N11.
- **PR-17 (the template count pin).** Each task that adds mail templates raises `MAIL_TEMPLATE_IDS`' pinned count
  (`tests/unit/templated-mail-channel.test.ts`, today `:128`) and the render test's `SAMPLE` in the same commit: N9 → 21,
  N14 → 23 (O2_REFUND_DUE, O2_REFUND_REMINDER), N17 → 24 (M12). Count the real list at that task; never guess.
- **PR-18 (the hosted-payment helpers).** `apps/api/src/billing/hosted-payment.ts` (N12: `paidOrAlmost`, `stillPayable`,
  `bestPaymentId`, `readPaymentStatus` (writes the `status_read` row), `startHostedCharge` (widen `operation` to include
  `"checkout"` in N18), `closeUnpaidHostedCharge`, `assertCurrentAgreement`, `recordCardAgreement`, `servedByNetopia`) and
  N12's `sealPaymentUrl`/`openPaymentUrl` in `records.ts` are the one implementation. **N13, N16 and N18 reuse them**: N18
  does not add its own `recordFailedStart`/`readOpenPayment` or a second seal pair; where N18's text has its own version, the
  executor maps it onto these helpers (same behaviour, the spec's §2.6.3 table) and says so in the report.
- **PR-19 (owner refs in tests are uuids).** Every billing `owner_ref` is a `uuid` (0085) and the settlements call
  `billing.owner_erasure_pending(uuid)`: N11's test owner refs (`n11-${label}-${uuid}`) become plain `randomUUID()`.
- **PR-20 (partial refunds need N6's schema, folded into N6).** N6's re-keyed unique indexes on `billing.charge_event`
  (the successors of 0086's `charge_event_transaction_kind_unique` and `charge_event_charge_transaction_kind_unique`) add
  `AND NOT (payment_provider = 'netopia' AND kind = 'REFUNDED')` to their WHERE, and the replaced refund-sum trigger's
  early return for a repeated (system, payment, kind) applies only when `NOT (NEW.payment_provider = 'netopia' AND
  NEW.kind = 'REFUNDED')`, so several REFUNDED parts on one NETOPIA payment are allowed and every part still passes the sum
  guard. N6's integration suite pins two REFUNDED parts on one NETOPIA payment (accepted) and a part that would exceed the
  payment (refused). — Why: spec §2.12.2 item 4 (a partial record keeps the rest open). — Cost if wrong: N14's split refunds
  refused by the database.
- **PR-21 (the tax summary counts NETOPIA sales, owned by N10).** N10 adds one step: `quarterSummaryRows` takes the payment
  system `{provider, environment}` instead of the bare environment; its SQL filters `charge.payment_provider = $provider AND
  charge.payment_environment = $environment`; the live summary (`liveQuarterSummaryRows`, `tax-summary.ts`) asks for
  `{provider: "netopia", environment: "live"}`; the xMoney callers that remain pass `{provider: "xmoney", environment}` until
  N23. Test: a NETOPIA sale appears in the summary of its own environment and not in the other. — Why: N6 kept the xMoney
  filter; no task owned the switch. — Cost if wrong: the owner's tax summary would show no NETOPIA sale.
- **PR-22 (a new task N24b, before N23).** The suites that seed xMoney rows with `seedActiveSubscription` and move money
  through xMoney's refund, which N24 leaves green on the xMoney seams but N23 would break, move to NETOPIA in a task of
  their own, **N24b** (brief in the plan): `billing-withdrawal`, `billing-withdraw-command`, `billing-jobs` (the
  `XMONEY_REFUND` lease case → `PAYMENT_REFUND`), `billing-tax-summary`, `billing-dispute` (its real-PostgreSQL block),
  `billing-cancel-link`, `billing-erasure-survival`, `billing-subscription-actions`, and the unit suites
  `billing-other-system` and `billing-retry-timing` (their `{ provider: "xmoney" }` callers become NETOPIA's other
  environment). Build order: … N22 → N24 → **N24b** → N23 → N25.
- **PR-23 (the country table is verified, N2).** N2's ISO 3166-1 numeric codes were typed from memory. The N2 executor
  checks every numeric code against the Unicode CLDR file `common/supplemental/supplementalData.xml` (`territoryCodes`
  elements), read once with `gh api repos/unicode-org/cldr/contents/common/supplemental/supplementalData.xml --jq .content |
  base64 --decode` into a temporary file outside the repository (read-only use; nothing from it is executed or committed),
  fixes any mismatch, and states in the report how many codes were checked. Every always-blocked country of
  `countryPolicy` (RU 643, BY 112, CN 156, HK 344, MO 446, IR 364, KP 408, CU 192, SY 760, VE 862, VN 704) and RO 642 are
  pinned by name in N2's test. — Why: a wrong numeric code would let a card from a blocked country through, or block a good
  one. — Cost if wrong: the safety net is the test's pinned list.
- **PR-24 (accepted decisions of the drafts).** Accepted as written, each where its text says: N2's `notFoundCodes ["404"]`
  (the fake answers the same; N22's recording pins the real one); N3's loopback base for the dev fake only; N9's per-day
  count of QUARANTINED rejections in `pnpm billing:tax-summary` (there is no daily owner email; internet junk stays in the
  journal), its `preParsing` relabel to a private media type, the proxy forwarding `verification-token` only to the notify
  path (≤16 KiB), and no O4 or PARSE_FAILED O3 in the provider-only mode; N10's RECOVERED → CARD_SAVED, "no refund request
  and no refusal" = no REFUND_REQUESTED and no DUPLICATE_PAYMENT row, a `status_read` row per VERIFY read, PAID without amount
  or currency = `PAYMENT_AMOUNT_MISMATCH`; N12's closing an unpaid upgrade of another quote at once, and "can still buy";
  N13's 15 minutes from the first PAID/AUTHORIZED read and a refused adoption ending `CARD_CHECK_DEFERRED`; N14's split-refund
  follow-ups (a part runs none; the closing part runs them for the whole request), O2_REFUND_DUE always carrying the command,
  one reminder per UTC day listing all open refunds; N15's "second payment" reading and status 10's O3 once per charge; N16's
  fifth parameter `environment` on `dueStatusReads`, SUBMITTED renewals on the open schedule, the 24-hour close for hosted
  INITIAL and CARD_CHECK and the quote expiry for upgrades; N17's M12 in `maintenance.ts`'s look-ahead, "decided" = SUCCEEDED
  (or FAILED for a RENEWAL), the erasure-commit revocation; N18's schema-optional address fields required by
  `addressRequired`, `postcodeOptional` in `@debateai/contract`, the status read before the owner lock, the start in flight
  (60 s) answering `CHECKOUT_PENDING`, the bring-forward throttled to one per 20 s, `checkoutPaymentSignals` deleted by N23;
  N19's upgrade agreement naming the NEW plan's monthly total, its calling-code table (a native check goes on the go-live
  list); N20's English consent = the spec's sentence plus today's cancel sentence, the Romanian `continueToCard` = "Comandă cu
  obligație de plată" (Terms §12), counsel's English wording question on go-live row 24; N21's `--test-root` switch and its
  check classification; N22's raw capture plus a separate scrubber command, and its two SELECTs moved into `BillingRepository`
  with one integration case each in `billing-repository.test.ts`; N24's fake clock instead of the time-shifting wrapper in the
  stack; N25's `/var/tmp/netopia-capture` (the owner may choose another folder); C1–C4's names and choices.
- **PR-25 (N19 reads N13's card details).** The card page pre-fills from N13's `GET /v1/billing/subscription/card`
  (`BillingCardDetailsResponseSchema`); the UI client function may keep N19's name `getBillingCardDetails`. N19's other
  dependencies on N12/N13 (the agreement argument, `startCardChange`'s body) follow N12's and N13's contract as merged.
- **PR-26 (N23's extra duties found by N24).** Before N23 deletes `activeSubscriptionEvents`' `{ provider: "xmoney" }` option,
  N24b has moved its two callers. N23 also deletes the stack's inert xMoney connector members (`tests/support/billingStack.ts`:
  `xmoney`, `xmoneyEnvironment`, `xmoneyPrivateKey`, `xmoneyPublicKey`, `siteId`, `ownerDesk`'s `xmoney`/`xmoneyEnvironment`),
  the harness's `NO_XMONEY` stand-in and its `xmoney`/`xmoneyEnvironment` deps lines, and `apps/runner/src/dev-billing-fakes.ts`'
  `xmoney: null`; its guard lists those files until they are clean.
